official_source_inventory.source_name: Baltimore Police Department Open Data landing page
key_findings: Official BPD page points users to the Part 1 Crime dataset, arrests, 911 calls, and executive summary documents.
The page still warns that Part 1 Crime Incident Reports provided by Open Data Baltimore were impacted starting in May 2021 after the RMS transition.

official_source_inventory.role: primary city-overlay candidate for SRS-style Baltimore incidents
key_findings: Official city-owned ArcGIS Feature Service with accessInformation set to City of Baltimore / Baltimore City Police Department.
Item metadata says the dataset contains crime data up to 12/31/2024 under the Summary Reporting System.
Observed operational year coverage is 2011-2024, with scattered pre-2011 noise rows that should not be treated as reliable coverage.

official_source_inventory.role: official companion feed and future-facing research surface
key_findings: Official city-owned ArcGIS Feature Service with coverage starting 1/1/2022 through present.

Item metadata says the way BPD collects and reports data changed effective 1/1/2025, but the public NIBRS feed already backfills 2022-2024, creating an overlapping official contract rather than a clean cutover.

official_source_inventory.source_name: Baltimore Police Department Executive Summary week ending 12/28/2024
key_findings: Official city-owned PDF with citywide seven-day, twenty-eight-day, and year-to-date counts by offense.
Provides a stronger audit surface than validating the feed against itself.
Official BPD press release dated 2025-01-01 reports 2024 homicides of 201 and non-fatal shootings of 414.
These final annual counts do not fully match the current legacy feed snapshot, which still reports 199 homicides and 415 shootings for full-year 2024.

source_contract.companion_source_name: Baltimore NIBRS Group A Crime Data
source_contract.recommended_reason: Baltimore is now ready for a bounded 2024 offense-selective overlay under the legacy SRS feed. The packet-local loader reproduces the reviewed weekly reconciliation window cleanly for rape, robbery, aggravated_assault, and larceny, while murder, burglary, and motor_vehicle_theft remain blocked for explicit public-contract reasons.

dedupe_key_findings: Official data dictionary describes CCNumber as a unique identifier for the record.
Observed public rows repeat CCNumber across subtype rows and multiple victim rows, so CCNumber is usable as an incident identifier but not as a globally correct row-level dedupe key.
overlap_findings: Legacy SRS feed and NIBRS Group A feed both publish 2022-2024 rows.
The feeds are not directly interchangeable because the legacy feed behaves like a summary-style SRS publication surface while the NIBRS feed reflects multi-offense NIBRS-style reporting.

spatial_contract.primary_assignment_path: Use Latitude and Longitude from the official city feed and spatially join to block groups.
spatial_contract.spatial_note: Baltimore is not blocked on geography. The problem is offense counting and public-contract continuity, not coordinate availability.

murder.note: Official weekly PDF aligns exactly on the mapped row count before the small geocode loss.

rape.note: Direct mapping and exact weekly-PDF match.

robbery.rule: Use only Description = ROBBERY. Do not add ROBBERY - COMMERCIAL or ROBBERY - CARJACKING because those subtype rows duplicate CCNumbers already represented in the total robbery series.
robbery.note: Naive summation of all robbery-like descriptions overstates robbery badly.

burglary.note: Still materially above the official weekly PDF. Keep blocked.

larceny.rule: Count unique CCNumber across the family {LARCENY, LARCENY FROM AUTO}. Raw row counts overstate the larceny total because subtype rows and repeated rows coexist in the public feed.
larceny.note: Under the family-level unique-CCNumber rule the weekly-PDF gap collapses to one geocoded incident.

motor_vehicle_theft.note: Close but not exact against the official weekly PDF.

offense_mapping.nibrs_group_a_note: The official NIBRS Group A feed is valuable context but not the recommended production overlay object for AGS-style summary alignment. Public NIBRS rows are multi-offense and not hierarchy-comparable to the city’s published SRS-style annual summaries without additional Baltimore-specific aggregation logic.

headline_findings: Legacy SRS packet-local contract matches the official weekly executive summary closely for murder, rape, robbery, aggravated_assault, and larceny.
Burglary remains materially high and motor_vehicle_theft remains modestly high.

The legacy feed does not fully align to the official January 1, 2025 year-end public release: the public year-end release reports 201 homicides and 414 non-fatal shootings for 2024, while the current full-year legacy feed snapshot reports 199 homicides and 415 shootings.

judgment.minimum_unblock_change: Keep the current packet-local legacy loader, preserve the bounded 2024 weekly-window contract, and resolve the remaining homicide and motor_vehicle_theft annual-public mismatches before broadening the live offense set.

blockers.detail: Baltimore publishes both a legacy SRS feed through 2024-12-31 and a NIBRS Group A feed starting 2022-01-01. The overlap is official, not hypothetical.
The official BPD Open Data page still warns that Open Baltimore Part 1 Incident Reports were impacted beginning in May 2021 after the RMS transition.
The current full-year legacy feed does not exactly match the official 2024 year-end homicide and shooting counts.
